strategies.comments:
Other Options

Although Vibrava has access to coverage moves for some of its checks, like Superpower for Clefairy and Heat Wave for Wormadam-S, it does not have room to fit such specific tools without sacrificing the momentum of U-turn or the utility of Toxic.

Checks and Counters

Clefairy: Vibrava is totally walled by Clefairy and cannot wear Clefairy down on its own. Clefairy can use Knock Off and Encore to further disrupt Vibrava and take advantage of Vibrava's passivity to support its teammates with other utility moves.

Super Effective Attacks: Walrein and Glaceon take little damage from Vibrava and easily dispatch it with STAB Ice Beam. Shelgon can blow past Vibrava's physical bulk with Outrage and can use Rest and Sleep Talk to deal with Toxic from Vibrava. Raichu and Pikachu commonly run Hidden Power Ice and can OHKO Vibrava with it, though neither want to take an Earthquake while trying to switch in.

Special Attackers: Vibrava's special bulk is lower compared to its physical bulk, making it prone to special attackers like Grumpig and Mr. Mime, though they don't take U-turn or Earthquake well. Offensive Pelipper can overpower Vibrava with its STAB moves and take advantage of its immunity to Vibrava's Earthquake.

Opposing Walls: Vibrava's poor damage output invites in opposing walls looking to recover HP or support their teammates. Clefairy, Wormadam-S, and Ivysaur can absorb Toxic and wear down Vibrava with their utility moves. Cleric Leafeon and specially defensive Meganium have Heal Bell and Aromatherapy, respectively, to heal off Vibrava's Toxic and support their teammates. Staryu can absorb Toxic, stay healthy with Recover, and wear Vibrava down with Scald, Toxic, and burns.

Status: Chip damage from poison makes Vibrava worse as a wall even though it commonly switches in on Muk's Poison Jab. Wormadam-S and Hippopotas commonly carry Toxic and Solrock can use Will-O-Wisp, though Hippopotas and Solrock dislike taking Toxic in return.

Knock Off: Knock Off is good against Vibrava because it removes Vibrava’s Eviolite and therefore worsens its ability to take hits. Clefairy walls Vibrava and thus gets many opportunities to weaken it for its teammates. Physical attackers like Mienfoo, Persian, and Emolga can use Knock Off to soften Vibrava up for themselves or their teammates.

movesets.name: Defensive
movesets.description:
Vibrava's Ground immunity, resistances to Rock and Poison, and reliable recovery backed by decent bulk with Eviolite let it take on common physical attackers like Lairon, Muk, and Arbok. Vibrava's role compression carves a niche in the presence of otherwise better Pokemon; Mienfoo is a great offensive check to Lairon but struggles against Muk, Arbok can set up on Muk but lacks Vibrava's longevity to take repeated hits from Lairon, and Hippopotas is a sturdier wall to physically offensive Rock- and Poison-types but lacks U-turn to gain momentum against its checks. Earthquake is generally Vibrava's better STAB move because it comes off its higher Attack and hits important targets for more damage, targeting Muk's lower Defense, 2HKOing Arbok even after Intimidate or a Coil boost, and guaranteeing an OHKO against Simisear after Stealth Rock damage. Earth Power is slightly weaker and comes off of Vibrava's lower Special Attack but hits physically bulkier foes like Lairon and Pawniard harder. U-turn lets Vibrava keep up momentum against Pokemon that would otherwise check it, such as Clefairy, Leafeon, and Glaceon. Toxic wears down Ground-immune Pokemon like Solrock, Emolga, and Vullaby and lets Vibrava put opposing walls like Frillish and Hippopotas on a timer.

Clefairy is one of the best partners for Vibrava, absorbing Toxic for it, supporting its status vulnerability with Heal Bell, and complementing its physical bulk with special bulk. Opposing Clefairy also totally walls Vibrava and leaves it reliant on teammates like Muk, Mienfoo, and Raichu to deal with Clefairy. Choice Scarf Mienfoo in particular appreciates having Vibrava as the primary resistance to Rock-type moves like Head Smash, as Mienfoo struggles to check Lairon without Eviolite. Poison-types like Muk and Ivysaur benefit from Vibrava luring Grass-types in for them, and they provide Vibrava with a teammate that absorbs Toxic. Muk stands out as a partner thanks to its immediate wallbreaking potential and Sticky Hold, allowing it to swap into Knock Off for Vibrava and threaten significant damage. Frail offensive Pokemon like Simisear, Persian, and Raichu appreciate being brought in freely by a slow U-turn. Meganium and Leafeon are excellent partners to Vibrava by covering for its status vulnerability with Aromatherapy and Heal Bell, respectively, while they benefit from Vibrava dealing with Poison-types like Muk and Arbok.
